_rule: Describe what THAT camera can see, and omit what it cannot. Palette and material words are IDENTITY and are byte-identical across all eight; only anatomy and framing words change. A rear camera is never told about a beard, a face, or the belt medallion — E01 measured that a shared prompt asking for 'a long red beard, gold necklace' on every view put a face on the back of the head at both 0.92 and 0.75 denoise, and that per-view prompting alone took face detections 1 -> 0 with silhouette held at IoU 0.784.
_orientation: Measured, not assumed: the sword tip sits at std-frame X -0.150, Y -0.156, so the greatsword is held FORWARD and on the character's RIGHT. Camera yaw N here equals turn_render view yaw N. yaw 90 = camera at +X = his LEFT flank (sword on the far side). yaw 270 = camera at -X = his RIGHT flank (sword side, nearest camera). yaw 45/315 = front three-quarters (315 is the sword side, and the blade crosses frame centre). yaw 135/225 = back three-quarters. el +55 = camera 55 deg above, so the crown and the tops of the pauldrons dominate and the face is strongly foreshortened.
_negative_is_constant: watermark, text, logo, blurry, photo, deformed — held identical across all eight so that per-view POSITIVE prompting is the only variable, which is the form E01 actually measured.
